articleBlocks: At first, this looked more like food and color phrases than one repeated-word pattern.
Tea pushed me in that direction immediately.
Salad kept that read alive for a moment, but with envy still did not sound right.
That was the moment the first idea stopped working.
Then With envy made the missing word much harder to miss.
Readings like Green tea and Green salad finally sounded exact instead of approximate.
The answer was Words that come after green.
Light and With envy then felt like confirmations, not extra mysteries.
Looking back, the whole pattern feels obvious in the best way.
solutionNarrative: Tea and Salad first pulled me toward food and color phrases, so that was the first path I tested. It held together for a moment, but with envy never really fit it. The more I pushed that first read, the more the board sounded stitched together instead of naturally solved.

The solve turned when I let with envy lead instead of treating it like an outlier. I tested Green tea and Green salad in my head, and those readings sounded like ordinary language. That moved me from guessing a topic to checking one repeatable word slot.

Then I used Revolution, Light, and With envy as the confirmation round. Green revolution, Green light, and Green with envy all sounded like phrases people would actually say, so I was no longer relying on the first pair of clues. The answer was Words that come after green.
